exposure: Gestational age at elective cesarean section (38, 39, or 40 weeks)
gestational age at elective cesarean sections
Infants born at 38 weeks vs. 39 weeks vs. 40 weeks gestation
Infants born by elective cesarean section
cohort: 952 infants born at 38-40 weeks gestation by elective cesarean section
finding: Postponing elective cesarean sections to later gestational ages, specifically beyond 39 weeks, may lead to improved infant growth and psychomotor development by 6 months of age.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight was significantly higher in the 40-week group compared to the 38 and 39-week groups.
